title: Art Shows
description: Read a leaflet and an entertainment programme the way you read them in the street: five questions (what, when, where, how much, how do I get in), a line read across, a price list read by category, and conditions such as "ages 12-19" or "no need to book" — with the words a programme uses (foyer, refreshments, interactive, performance, to book, free, venue, guided tour, exhibition, box office) and the times it prints, am for ante meridiem and pm for post meridiem. Then describe in fewer words with compound adjectives (science-inspired, stone-walled, naturally-produced, bright-coloured, elephant-training, a 200-page book, a one million-year-old tree), with their three rules — the hyphen, the noun that never takes -s, and the unpacking after be. Take part in a class discussion: tell a fact from an opinion, give yours and support it with a reason, agree and disagree politely, judge a film with wit, shot, adept, thought-provoking and to tackle a subject. Hear where an English word puts its stress (-ion, -ic and -ity pull it forward, a compound noun stresses its first word). And close on Strings: James Joyce, the five senses of the word string, literal against figurative, and the rhyme schemes a b a b and c d c d, plus the word list of a Ray Charles biography
